These are processed through a shared CNN architecture to produce 20-dimensional embeddings. The triplet loss enforces that embeddings of same-player, same-role pairs are closer than those of different players or roles. Role-conditioning via K-means clustering ensures that stylistic differences within roles are preserved while allowing cross-role comparisons. Augmentation via 3-phase combinations increases dataset diversity, improving generalization. The system's dual nature—embedding and classification—is unified under a single objective: minimizing intra-class variance while maximizing inter-class separation. Failure modes include poor heatmap quality, ambiguous role assignments, and insufficient training diversity leading to overfitting or misclassification.
